title: History (Ancient, Medieval & Modern)
intro: History is the single largest GA block in SSC, and it rewards organised memory rather than cleverness. Hold three timelines in your head — Ancient (Indus to the Guptas), Medieval (Delhi Sultanate and the Mughals), and Modern (British rule and the freedom struggle) — and anchor each to a few dates, rulers and events. The questions are direct: who, when, where. This chapter gives you those anchors topic by topic so revision is fast and the marks are reliable.

items.name: Kalinga War
items.formula: 261 BCE — Ashoka, then turned to Buddhism

topics.name: Ancient India
topics.details: The Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilisation (c. 2600–1900 BCE) was a Bronze-Age, town-planned culture; key sites include Harappa and Mohenjo-daro. The Mauryan Empire (322 BCE, Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chanakya) peaked under Ashoka; the Gupta Age is called the 'Golden Age'.

solved.problem: After which war did Ashoka embrace Buddhism?

unsolved.problem: Name a major Indus Valley city on the Indus river.
The Gupta period is famous as the ___ Age.
Which dynasty did Ashoka belong to?
How many Vedas are there?
In which year was the Kalinga War fought?

topics.name: Medieval India
topics.details: The Delhi Sultanate began in 1206 (Qutb-ud-din Aibak, Slave dynasty) and ran through the Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi dynasties. The Mughal Empire was founded by Babur after the First Battle of Panipat (1526); Akbar consolidated it, Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal.

solved.problem: Who founded the Mughal Empire and after which battle?
solved.solution: Babur, after the First Battle of Panipat (1526).
Shah Jahan, in memory of Mumtaz Mahal, at Agra.

solved.problem: Who founded the Delhi Sultanate (Slave dynasty)?
Which Mughal emperor is associated with the Din-i-Ilahi?

unsolved.problem: In which year was the First Battle of Panipat fought?
Name the last major dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.
The Taj Mahal is located in which city?
Akbar belonged to which empire?
The famous south-Indian empire with capital Hampi was?

topics.name: Modern India & Freedom Struggle
topics.details: British dominance began with Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764). The Revolt of 1857 is the First War of Independence; the INC was founded in 1885. Gandhi led the major movements, and India became independent on 15 August 1947.

solved.problem: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
solved.solution: 1885 (its first president was W. C. Bonnerjee).

solved.problem: The Dandi Salt March (1930) was part of which movement?
solved.solution: The Civil Disobedience Movement, led by Gandhi.

solved.problem: Which battle (1757) marked the start of British rule in Bengal?
Who was India's first Prime Minister?

unsolved.problem: The Revolt of 1857 is also called the ___ War of Independence.
In which year did the Quit India Movement begin?
On what date did India gain independence?
Gandhi's first satyagraha in India (1917) was at?
The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in which year?

topics.name: Post-Independence India
topics.details: After 1947, Sardar Patel (the 'Iron Man') integrated the princely states. The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President. India fought wars in 1962, 1965 and 1971 (the last creating Bangladesh).

solved.problem: Who integrated the princely states into India?
solved.solution: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the first Home Minister.

solved.problem: When did the Constitution of India come into force?
Who was the first President of India?
The 1971 war led to the creation of which country?

unsolved.problem: Sardar Patel is popularly called the ___ of India.
India became a Republic on which date?
The 1962 war was fought with which country?
The movement that boosted food-grain output in the 1960s?
States were reorganised on which basis in 1956?

shortcuts: Tie each era to 2–3 dates and rulers; SSC asks "who/when", not analysis.
Panipat 1526 = Mughals begin; Plassey 1757 = British begin; 1885 = Congress.
Ashoka → Maurya → Buddhism after Kalinga (261 BCE).
mistakes: Mixing up who built the Taj Mahal (Shah Jahan) with Akbar.
Swapping the dates of Independence (1947) and the Republic (1950).
Forgetting the Rigveda is the oldest Veda.
pyq: SSC Tier 1 leans on modern history and the freedom struggle (Gandhi's movements, key dates) plus a couple of ancient/medieval anchors (Maurya, Gupta, Mughal). Dates and "founder of" questions dominate.

flashcards.q: Battle that began British rule in Bengal?

summary: Organise history into three timelines and anchor each to dates, rulers and events: Maurya (322 BCE) and Gupta in the ancient era; the Delhi Sultanate (1206) and Mughals (1526) in the medieval; Plassey (1757), 1857, Congress (1885), Gandhi's movements and Independence (1947) in the modern. Direct "who/when" recall wins the marks.
